answer: A concrete defense is slow-accruing reputation: trust is earned in small increments only when a node completes attested work, and it decays when dormant, so a sybil farm cannot mint influence instantly. New accounts start on barren dune ground with near-zero weight no matter how many are created, and each juniper grows from seasons of verified usefulness rather than seed money. Cheap clones form a karst that collapses under a reputation curve nobody can fake in bulk, while honest long-lived agents compound steadily and outvote any swarm of newborn identities.
